supporting_observations.claim: Near the reported time, WS-MLOPEZ-01 obtained service tickets for FILE-HD-01 under its machine account. These records do not identify a PowerShell process, script, or initiating administrator.
At 13:44:40 UTC, the workstation established a proxy tunnel to download.windowsupdate.com using a Windows-Update-Agent user agent and received approximately 38.8 MB.

The Windows Update transfer is consistent with the supplied business-hours patching context, but does not establish that the reported PowerShell window ran the approved patch script or was initiated by omar.haddad.

A short-lived console-host process was recorded at 14:12:25–14:12:27 UTC, substantially later than the reported window. Its records identify csrss.exe as parent and do not identify a PowerShell command.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied evidence contains no PowerShell process-creation, command-line, script-block, or module-logging record for the reported execution around 13:40 UTC.
The supplied evidence does not provide a remote-logon or execution chain linking WS-OHADDAD-01 and omar.haddad to the reported window.
Kerberos service-ticket records identify the machine account and target service, not the accessed script or executing process (T024-00067, T024-00072).
The Windows Update record is a tunnel summary rather than inspected request or payload evidence, and does not link the transfer to PowerShell (T024-00113).
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually executed around 13:40 UTC and, if so, its command, parent process, user, and execution outcome.
Whether the reported window resulted from authorized execution of \\FILE-HD-01\IT\Deploy-Patches.ps1 by omar.haddad from WS-OHADDAD-01.
Whether the alerted activity involved malicious code, persistence, credential theft, or data exfiltration.
Whether the later console-host process was related to the reported window (T024-00285 through T024-00288).

Obtain remote-execution and authentication records from WS-OHADDAD-01 and WS-MLOPEZ-01, including WinRM or WMI logs where available, to identify the initiating host and account.
Retrieve FILE-HD-01 share-access auditing for IT\Deploy-Patches.ps1 and the script's contents, integrity information, and execution logs.
Confirm with omar.haddad whether this workstation was patched at the reported time and obtain the corresponding deployment record.
